problem:
The following table shows the number of customers per minute, $C(t),$ that arrive at a bank, measured over a period of $15$ minutes.

| $t\,\text{(minutes)}$ | $0$ | $3$ | $7$ | $12$ | $15$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $C(t)\,\text{(customers/minute)}$ | $3$ | $4$ | $3$ | $5$ | $2$ |

Use the right Riemann sum over $[0,15]$ with four subintervals to approximate the total number of customers served.

feedback.problem:
The following table shows some values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the interval $[-2,19].$

| $x$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $7$ | $12$ | $19$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $5$ | $9$ | $11$ | $20$ |

Use the left Riemann sum, with the four subintervals indicated by the data, to approximate the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ over the interval $[-2,19].$
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, we have $n=4$ rectangles. Using the left Riemann sum, the area is approximated as

$$
A≈f(-2)Δ{x}_{1}+f(1)Δ{x}_{2}+f(7)Δ{x}_{3}+f(12)Δ{x}_{4},
$$

where each $Δ{x}_{i}$ is calculated by considering the step between a particular $x$-value and the next one, i.e.,

$$
Δ{x}_{i}={x}_{i+1}-{x}_{i}.
$$

We set up a value table that includes the $Δx$'s.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $1$ | $7$ | $12$ | $19$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $Δx$ | $3$ | $6$ | $5$ | $7$ | $-$ |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $5$ | $9$ | $11$ | $20$ |

Finally, we plug in the numbers to approximate the area under the curve and get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈1\cdot 3+5\cdot 6+9\cdot 5+11\cdot 7 \\  & =3+30+45+77 \\  & =155.\end{aligned}
$$
